in_arabic.name: أَثَى
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مؤنث يعني الثناء الحسن أو الذكر الجميل
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أَثَى هو اسم مؤنث مشتق من الفعل أَثَى يَأثِي أَثاءً، ويعني الثناء الحسن أو الذكر الجميل. وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأنعام: 'وَأَثَاءً لَّهُ مُكَرِمِينَ'، الآية ٨٨، أي تكريمًا له بالإِجلال والتعظيم. ويُستخدم هذا الاسم في الثقافة الإسلامية للإشارة إلى الفتاة التي تتميز بالشخصية الحميدة والمجتمعية الرفيعة.

in_urdu.name: اثا
in_urdu.long_meaning: اثا ایک مؤنث نام ہے جو کہ عربی زبان کے فعل اثا سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے ثنا حسن یا اچھا ذکر۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں لڑکیوں کے لئے مقبول ہے، خاص طور پر پاکستان اور بھارت میں۔ اس نام کا روحانی مطلب ہے کہ لڑکی جو اچھی کردار اور عظیم اخلاق کی مالک ہو.

in_hindi.name: अथा
in_hindi.long_meaning: अथा एक सुंदर और अर्थपूर्ण नाम है जो कि इस्लामी परंपरा में प्रयोग होता है। यह नाम अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है और इसका अर्थ है अच्छी प्रतिष्ठा या सुंदर ذكر। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम लड़कियों के लिए पसंद किया जाता है क्योंकि यह नाम उनके अच्छे चरित्र और उच्च नैतिक मूल्यों को दर्शाता है।

in_pashto.name: اثا
in_pashto.long_meaning: اثا د ښځو یو نوم دی چی د عربی ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، مان یې ښه ثنا یا نیک ذکر دی. په افغانستان او پاکستان کې د پښتنو او نورو مذهبونو تر منځ دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کیږي کوم چي ښه کرکتر او سلوک لري.

in_english.name: Atha
in_english.long_meaning: Atha is a feminine given name of Arabic origin, derived from the verb 'atha', which means to praise or to mention with good words. In Islamic tradition, the name Atha signifies a person with a good character and high moral values. It is mentioned in the Quran in Surah An'am: 'And they will be honored with dignified reverence.' The name Atha is popular across Muslim cultures, symbolizing a person with a beautiful reputation and kind heart.

pronunciation.pashto: په پښتو کې د تلفظ تفصیل: ا-ثا

data.cultural_impact: The name "Atha" is derived from Arabic language, a semitic language spoken primarily in the Muslim world, including Middle Eastern and North African countries. In a cultural context, the name "Atha" signifies a gift, bestowed upon an individual by God Almighty. In many Muslim communities, the value of giving and receiving gifts is deeply engrained in their way of life. The concept of a gift from God highlights the belief in divine providence and the idea that life's blessings are ultimately derived from God.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name "Atha" represents the belief in submission to God and the idea that every blessing, every gift, every favor, and every success is a manifestation of His mercy and divine plan. In Islamic tradition, it is believed that God is the giver of all good things and that true happiness and peace come from recognizing and being grateful for His gifts, both material and spiritual. The name "Atha" serves as a constant reminder of this fundamental truth and reinforces the belief in the ultimate sovereignty of God over all aspects of human life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Given" symbolizes Gift from God. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Atha serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of given.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah, Chapter 5. Discusses Atha' Al-Khuldan as a sub-tribe of the Banu Tamim living in the Hejaz region, Arabia.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun was a renowned historian and sociologist. He wrote an extensive work known as 'Muqaddimah', which includes discussions on various topics including geography, history, and sociology. In Chapter 5, he mentions Atha' Al-Khuldan, a sub-tribe of the Banu Tamim, specifically located in the Hejaz region of Arabia.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hazm's Al-Fasihah. Describes Atha as a city and the name of its people in the region of Bashr, Yemen.
historical_references.context: Ibn Hazm was a prominent scholar, jurist, and poet during the Almohad Caliphate in Spain. In his book 'Al-Fasihah', he writes about various topics including history, literature, and linguistics. He mentions a city called 'Atha' and its people in the region of Bashr, Yemen.
